The real persist driver executes checked Create/Write(image)/Sync/Release actions. Reply release checks the actual receipt against the operation and complete request. Runtime::begin_election derives a checked next-term self-vote; the caller persists it before campaign and outbound sends. Each real call retains its peer/request in VoteCall, and its returned Result reaches Tally::complete_call. Tally records all matching-context completions, including errors/refusals/obsolete replies, and only counts distinct in-range matching-term grants. Machine::elect checks the live candidate's identity, membership, term, self-vote and majority. Runtime records the leader transition, and the parent proves those facts for each successful recorded entry.

Higher-term reply coverage: the actual continuation invokes prepare_term with the responding peer and reply. A valid greater term immediately changes the core to follower with no vote, increments the operation serial safely, and constructs an owned new-term image/context. The operation gate remains held through persist. finish_term consumes a checked receipt and validates the image, serial, identity and current state. Storage errors release no response or promotion from that continuation. Old quorums cannot promote in the new term. The parent proves immediate step-down and the exact submitted image. The local term-completion relation still needs its earlier-submission and actual host-effect linkage; an owned token is not by itself a durability theorem.

No absent global relation was replaced by a permissive or empty definition.

Snapshot/recovery coverage: no compaction or application snapshot decoder exists. Nonempty snapshot files are rejected; truncated or undecodable state stops recovery instead of forgetting a vote. Validated vote/term images recover a follower with empty pending context and a fresh journal. Local recovery exclusion lemmas are conditional on the saved image. The pinned simulator preserves completed writes across node restart; sync_all is a no-op and power_fail is unfinished. Truncate/write has an interruption gap; no multi-file atomicity or real-disk crash consistency is assumed. Consensus decisions remain in checked source; async composition and host-call preconditions are not declared exempt.
